Research program · New York City

Reading the Housing Record

A deed amount, a financing label, and a tax liability may look like simple facts. These papers ask what each field actually measures—and how tax rules shape the transactions we observe.

Three papers, separate claims

The studies use related New York City records. Each has its own sample, question, and validation requirements. Public versions and replication materials are linked below.

Research map

What the records can tell us

Recorded amount

Is it a market price?

The deed study isolates lender-acquisition transfers whose consideration can have a legal meaning distinct from a sale price.

Recorded financing

Who is being compared?

The house study tests how buyer and transaction composition affect the observed cash–mortgage contrast.

Statutory rules

Where do sales shift?

The tax study calculates legal liabilities and compares transaction patterns before and after the 2019 reform.

Validation status

What is still being checked

Two independent readers have yet to complete the blinded instrument review for the house paper and the probability-sample deed review for the foreclosure paper. Classification error, uncertainty, and any resulting reruns will be reported after those reviews. The current public papers should be read with those checks outstanding.

The tax paper's statutory calculations and reform comparison do not depend on these document audits. Its revised submission draft is undergoing author review; the Zenodo link points to the public preprint.
